# @uaudio/luna-builder-sdk

> TypeScript/JavaScript SDK for LUNA Add Ons. One `Luna` namespace. Props (`.value`, `.onChange`, `.set`), Collections (`.items`, `.byId`, `.onChange`). Runs inside LUNA (WebSocket, `?port=` on the page URL) or in a browser talking to LUNA on localhost.

Not supported: streaming audio. The SDK edits the session (MIDI clips and notes, audio clips,
parameters, transport), plays live MIDI messages on a track or out of a MIDI device
(`Luna.SendMidi`, `Luna.QwertyMidi`), and receives live MIDI from the MIDI devices LUNA sees
(`Luna.MidiInput`). For live MIDI input always use `Luna.MidiInput`, not Web MIDI
(`navigator.requestMIDIAccess()`): LUNA's macOS web view has no Web MIDI, and `Luna.MidiInput` hears the devices LUNA's MIDI settings list, the same way inside LUNA and in a browser.

Start with QUICKSTART, then the API page for the object you are using. Use EVIDENCE when
the engine does something the docs do not say. Use PROTOCOL only for the raw escape hatch.

## Docs

- [Quickstart](QUICKSTART.md): connect, session, props, tracks, controls, clips, effects, markers, chords, workspace, gui, errors, testing.
- [Files guide](FILES-GUIDE.md): a walkthrough of the file routes for developers new to them: which route to pick, recipes for pick/drop/folders/media-by-path, making one page work in LUNA and a browser, and a common-mistakes table. Read it before FILES.md if the routes are unfamiliar.
- [Files](FILES.md): getting a user's file into an Add On. File route (`<input type="file">`, HTML drop, `uploadFile`) vs path route (`chooseFiles`, `onPathDrop`, `importPath`); never mix them. `luna.gui.serveMediaFile(addOnId, path)` turns an audio or video path into a URL the page plays.
- [Clips](CLIPS.md): drawing and editing clips, waveforms, MIDI notes, fades and crossfades as LUNA does. Read it before any timeline or clip-editing code: compiled clips (not raw clips), per-piece renderings, moving and crossfading overlapping clips, selection, an interactive editor, testing.
- [Recipes](RECIPES.md): thirteen Add Ons to ask an agent for, and the SDK each one leans on.
- [Manifest](MANIFEST.md): `manifest.json` fields (`target`, `floating`, `show_with_session`, `fixed_size`, `run_hidden`, ...), Add Ons folder, how LUNA loads a page, secrets (`luna.secrets`).
- [Protocol](PROTOCOL.md): verbs, paths, correlation, pushes, error codes, where things live.
- [Evidence](EVIDENCE.md): numbered measured facts about engine behaviour; cite as "fact N".
- [Tree snapshot](tree/luna-3.0.0.15776.json): the shape of the nodes the SDK builds on, for one LUNA build. `ua-builder tree <path>` prints any node's shape; `ua-builder tree --out file.json` snapshots the running build.

## API reference (generated)

- [api/index.md](api/index.md): every exported class, function and type in the Luna namespace.

## Skills (Claude Code)

- skills/create-add-on: ask the target, scaffold, connect, first feature, tests.
- skills/add-feature: wrap an engine path the SDK does not type yet.
- skills/test-add-on: MockEngine fixtures, settled(), live lane rules.
- skills/debug-connection: nothing connects, no pushes, wrong port, reconnect.
- skills/verify-add-on: prove an Add On against a running LUNA from a second client, and check the undo queue.
- skills/edit-clips: draw and edit clips, waveforms, MIDI notes, fades and crossfades; the steps and pitfalls of CLIPS.md.

These six ship as the `ua-luna-builder` plugin (`plugins/ua-luna-builder/`), which also
carries the SDK builds, the `ua-builder` CLI, the add-on-basic and add-on-typescript templates, the examples and
QUICKSTART/FILES/CLIPS/MANIFEST/PROTOCOL/EVIDENCE/RECIPES. Installed as a plugin, run the CLI as
`node <plugin-root>/sdk/cli.js <command>` instead of `npx ua-builder <command>`.

## Rules of thumb

- Await `luna.session()` before touching tracks. Call `track.loadStrip()` before reading gain/pan/mute.
- Nodes outside a session (`luna.gui.main`, `luna.preferences`) need `node.watch()` to follow pushes.
- Touch every control a user edits (fact 78): clicks are one-shot `set()`/`toggle()`, bracketed for you; drags use `Luna.bindRange(input, control)` for `<input type="range">` or `Luna.bindDrag(element, control)` for a div/canvas knob (touch, writes, release, following LUNA except mid-drag); `Luna.bindGesture` is the touch-and-release part alone for your own pointer code.
- Fader scales: `control.taper.value` is a `Luna.Taper` on gain-type controls (`null` elsewhere): `toNormalized(db)` / `toDb(n)` use LUNA's own table, `marks()` (or `marks({ compact: true })`) the dB values LUNA draws hash marks at, the last being -144 (label it ∞). It changes when a summing console swaps the taper; LUNA keeps the dB and moves `normalized`, so redraw on `control.taper.onChange` (fact 134).
- DOM that is rebuilt (mixer strips): collect its listeners and bindings in a `Luna.Bindings` (`on`, `add`, `{ bindings }`), `clear()` it at the start of each rebuild, and schedule rebuilds with `whenIdle(render)` so none runs mid-drag.
- Keyboard: inside LUNA, any key the page does not `preventDefault()` goes on to LUNA's own shortcuts (fact 81). Call `Luna.bindShortcuts(luna)` after connecting so undo, redo, play and record also work outside LUNA; inside LUNA it installs nothing (facts 79-81).
- Timeline = ticks (96e9 per beat); source offsets = nanoseconds. No conversion in the SDK.
- Effect bypass is `slot.setIn(bool)`, not the `enabled` property.
- MIDI: `clip.midi.ready()`, then `clip.midi.notes` / `.events` are live lists in clip-relative ticks (`Note.startTick` 0 is the clip's start; add `clip.start.value` for a session tick; `lane.createNotes` takes session ticks but returns clip-relative notes, writes channel 0 only, and makes the clip if none is under the notes; `session.insertClip` needs a `sourceUid`, so it cannot make an empty MIDI clip; facts 111-112). Write with `clip.addNote`/`addNotes` (many notes, one undo step)/`addMidi`. These are clip edits. To play notes live, `const midi = new Luna.SendMidi(luna)`: `sendMidiNote(sessionUid, trackUid, note, velocity, noteOn)`, `sendMidi` (raw 3 bytes), `sendController`, `sendProgramChange`, `sendNoteToTracks`, `sendDeviceNote` (feeds a device's *input*), `sendAllNotesOff` (facts 108-109). To play MIDI hardware, `sendNoteToOutput(device, note, velocity, noteOn, channel?)`, `sendControllerToOutput`, `sendProgramChangeToOutput`, `sendMidiToOutput` take a `luna.midiDevices` entry with an `outputPort` (fact 124); `qwerty.handleKeyDownToOutput(e, device)` plays the computer keyboard there. `new Luna.QwertyMidi(midi)` maps A-; and W-P to notes (Z/X octave, C/V velocity) from `handleKeyDown(e, sessionUid, trackUid)` / `handleKeyUp(e)`; call `releaseAll()` on blur. To hear MIDI hardware live, `const input = new Luna.MidiInput(luna)`, then `input.listen(device | port | 'all', (m) => ...)` (after `luna.midiDevices.load()`) returns an unsubscribe (`examples/midi-input.html` is a whole page); each message has `type` (`noteOn`, `noteOff` (also note-on velocity 0), `controlChange`, `programChange`, `pitchBend`, `polyPressure`, `channelPressure`), `status`, `channel`, `data1`, `data2`, `time` (ms on LUNA's clock, compare between messages only) and `port`. `onNote(target, (note, velocity, on) => ...)` and `onControlChange(target, (cc, value) => ...)` filter; `{ onGap }` reports missed batches. Only channel messages, never what `SendMidi` sent; nothing flows until a listener subscribes; `engine.receiveMidi(device, [[status, d1, d2], ...])` drives it in the mock (fact 125).
- TypeScript, React or any bundler: `ua-builder new <name> --template add-on-typescript`. It builds `src/` into one classic IIFE script (`dist/main.js`; Windows blocks module scripts under `file://`), types the `Luna` global through tsconfig `"types": ["@uaudio/luna-builder-sdk/global"]` (do not import the SDK in `src/`), and `npm run pack` builds then packs without sources, source maps, configs or `.env`. `ua-builder pack` refuses a page whose scripts are missing.
- Files (FILES.md): if the page needs the audio, use `<input type="file">` or an HTML `drop`, which give `File`s in LUNA and a browser alike, then `session.uploadFile({ bytes: file })`. `uploadFile` and `importPath` add a source to the session **without a clip** (it appears in `session.sources`); place it with `session.insertClip` only if wanted. `luna.gui.chooseFiles()` and `Luna.onPathDrop()` give **paths the page cannot read**; they only feed `session.importPath(path)` (a source) or `session.importFile(path)` (LUNA's import, with a clip), an optimization that skips copying through the page. Never `chooseFiles` and then try to `fetch` the path. The exception is audio and video: `luna.gui.serveMediaFile(addOnId, path)` answers a URL the page plays (`<video src>`) or reads with XMLHttpRequest (fact 114), which is how an Add On reloads a media file whose path it saved in `session.storage`. In LUNA 3.1.0.4589 and earlier (macOS) `<input type="file">` opens nothing (its `cancel` fires at once) and path drops stop after the Add On window is reopened (facts 104-105): always offer an HTML drop zone, and `chooseFiles` + `importPath` for paths.
- Session storage (fact 129): `session.storage.context(name)` keeps data with the session, at `<context>/<record>/<field>` = any JSON. `add` a field before `set`; pass `{ undoable: true }` for edits that belong in undo. The context is any name without `/`, not only the Add On id: use your id plus a suffix per kind of data (`com.example.seq.tracks`, `com.example.seq.view`), a record per item (a track uid) and a field per part (`pattern`, `channel`). Do not store a whole record as one value: each `set` replaces the value whole, and one value cannot mix undoable and non-undoable parts. (Before 0.3.0 this was `session.preferences`, with preferences and properties; see CHANGELOG.)
- Secrets (MANIFEST.md, "Secrets"): API keys and tokens go in `luna.secrets.get/set/delete(name)`, which inside LUNA uses the OS keychain scoped to the Add On's `id`; never `localStorage`, IndexedDB, cookies or a file in the Add On. Outside LUNA (`luna.secrets.storage === 'memory'`) values last until reload.
- `/gui` is absent on a headless engine: check `luna.gui.available()`; without it every `luna.gui` command and `importFile` reject with `Luna.Unsupported`.
- Sends are outputs: `channel.outputs.byId('send_0')`, with `assign`/`unassign`/`retarget`/`moveTo`. Assign appends, so use `retarget` to replace (fact 43). Read `send.destinations` (each has the assignment `uid` that `unassign` takes, `busUid`, `name`, `error`), not the raw `assignments` rows (fact 83).
- Pan is `pan` on a mono channel and `pan_left`/`pan_right` on a stereo one (fact 84): use `output.pans` (or `panLeft`/`panRight`); `output.pan` is the left one on stereo.
- Automation values go on the wire as float literals (`Luna.float`), because LUNA stores a bare whole number as 0 (fact 82). `lane.insert`/`setValue`/`move`/`clear` resolve once the lane shows the edit.
- Plugins: `slot.setPlugin(id)` and `channel.insert(id)` resolve once loaded (`slot.loaded`) and reject with the slot's `plugin_error`; list parameters with `slot.params`, which leaves out a cleared plugin's ghosts (fact 86).
- Presets: `luna.presets.query({ pluginId, search, tags, matchAnyTag, withTags })` filters by name and tags (fact 120); `luna.presets.tagGroups(pluginId)` gives the tag chips by group; `luna.presets.recommend(pluginId, text)` asks UA Assistant (needs `luna.assistant.enabled`, and the plugin instantiated since it connected; fact 121); `slot.loadPreset(uid)` loads one onto an effect (fact 122). For a search box, tag chips and recommendations together use `luna.presets.selection(pluginId)`: set `search`/`tags`, read `presets`/`recommendations`; it debounces and drops overtaken replies. `examples/presets.html` is the whole page. Track presets: `luna.presets.trackSelection({ category })` (categories are tags, `Luna.TRACK_PRESET_CATEGORIES`; All and Instrument also list installed instrument plugins' presets, `row.isInstrumentPreset`, with `row.pluginName`), `session.newTrackFromPreset(row)` resolves to the new tracks, `track.loadPreset(row)` replaces a track's preset, `track.presetUid` marks it (fact 132); `examples/track-presets.html` is the whole flow.
- A removed object is disposed: `node.disposed`, `node.onDispose(fn)`; its commands reject with `Luna.Disposed`.
- Bounce/export: `session.bounce({ channelUids, range })` and `session.exportMain()` return a `Render`; watch `render.progress` and `await render.done()` (fact 44).
- Clips and fades (CLIPS.md, skills/edit-clips): draw, hit-test and select the segments of `await lane.compiledClips.load()` / `lane.compiledClips.inOrder()`, never `lane.clips`, which overlap (fact 116). Drag with `seg.move(toTick)` (LUNA splits or trims the clip beneath; `clip.move` moves the whole span and any clip on top of it, fact 119); crossfade at an edit with `seg.crossfade(next, len)`, which covers overlapping clips (fact 117). Fades exist on audio clips only (the SDK refuses others; LUNA silently ignores them). `seg.needsRender` true with no rendering means LUNA is re-rendering: hold the last waveform. Draw fades after all segments. Inside LUNA, draw resize and edge pointers as SVG images (fact 118).
- Waveforms: `Luna.compiledClipAudio(timeline, seg, clip, session.sources)` says which audio a segment plays (the file, or LUNA's rendering of that piece; LUNA renders time-stretched clips, clips with effects and files at another sample rate, piece by piece); `Luna.clipAudio(clip, ...)` only suits a clip nothing overlaps; `new Luna.Waveforms().range(source, startNs, stopNs, Luna.kindForScale(nsPerPixel))` pages the pairs; `Luna.audioNsAtTick(timeline, seg, audio, tick)` maps a tick to a file offset (facts 72-73, 116); `Luna.waveformColumns(range, width, nsAt, { gain })` (LUNA's gain is `session.context.waveformZoom.value` times the clip gain; fact 94) gives one min/max per pixel per channel, reduced as LUNA's timeline does (linear, touching zero, interpolated when zoomed in; fact 93), `Luna.waveformLanes` stacks a lane per channel, so stereo is never folded to one shape, and `Luna.traceWaveform(ctx, channel, lane, x0)` adds LUNA's filled outline to a path. `Luna.waveformPeak(range)` gives the gain to normalize. No analysis means draw an outline, never silence.
- Creating: `const [track] = await session.newTrack({...})` resolves to the new `Luna.Track`s (one per `count`) and `const clip = await session.insertClip({...})` to the new `Luna.Clip`, loaded: never diff `session.tracks` or find them by name. `insertClip` also takes `layer`, `lengthFollows` (`'ticks'`/`'time'`), `algType` and `copyOf: clip` (copies gain, fades, warps, MIDI; source, offsets and name default to that clip's). Inside a batch `transaction()` both resolve at once with `id` set and props `undefined` until the commit, so `insertClip({ trackUid: track.id })` on a track made in the same batch works (fact 135).
- MIDI edits: `midi.setVelocities` (one post, one undo entry), `midi.setMuted`, `midi.deleteNotes`. They move LUNA's selection and put it back (fact 74), and work inside a `transaction()`.
- Transactions: `session.transaction(name, fn)` is a batch, one undo step; rewrite notes there with `midi.deleteNotes(old)` then `clip.addNotes(new)`, and read the lists after it resolves (LUNA holds pushes until the commit). `{ continuous: true }` is a live gesture: each command replaces the one before, so write every step relative to the start; `lane.createNotes` in one regenerates a take and only the last is kept (fact 115). `lane.createNotes` refuses inside a batch.
- Recording: `luna.audioInputs()` lists device inputs; `session.record({ track, inputUid, startTick, seconds })` runs the whole pass and resolves to the finalized take, source listed (facts 75-76).
- MIDI devices: `luna.midiDevices` lists the MIDI devices LUNA sees (`name`, `midiDeviceType`, `lastMidiNote`, ...); filter on `isPhysical` to drop LUNA's `All` and `None` entries, and `watch()` it to follow hot-plugging. `device.outputPort?.uid` / `device.inputPort?.uid` are the engine's port uids; MIDI device uids change when LUNA restarts, so match devices by `name` (fact 123).
- `Luna.settle(predicate, what, { refresh })` is how to wait for an edit: LUNA answers `null` whether or not it happened (fact 71).
- Key and chords: `await session.musical.setKeySignature(sharpsAndFlats, isMinor, tick?)` resolves to the row (one per tick, fact 113); `musical.keySignatureAt(tick)` is the key in effect. `Luna.parseChord(name)` splits a chord symbol (lowercase roots accepted).
- Timeline conversions: `tickAtBar`, `tickAt({bar,beat,tick})`, `barBeat(tick)`, `seconds(tick)`, `tickAtSeconds(s)`, `formatBarBeat(tick)`; `timeline.onChange` fires on tempo or meter edits (`tempoMap.onChange` does not: an edit rewrites an existing event; `transport.tempo` follows only the playhead). Tempo reads throw `unavailable` until the tempo map loads (`timeline.tempoLoaded`); they never assume 120 BPM. `barBeat().tick` is engine ticks: pass it to `Luna.formatBarBeat` unconverted. `marker.barBeat` / `marker.seconds` are derived props that follow the marker and the tempo map.
- Folders outside a session (`/renders`, `/jobs`, `/plugins`) need `collection.watch()` before they follow pushes (fact 34).
- Tests: `Luna.MockEngine`, `await engine.settled()`, `await luna.settled()`.

## SDK feedback

When a workflow was harder than the SDK should make it, end your reply with the line
`LUNA BUILDER SDK FEEDBACK: <version>` (the version from `ua-builder doctor`, or
`Luna.VERSION`) followed by a prompt that can be used to update the SDK to support the
improved workflow.
